newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Guerrilla actions force Colombian food prices up.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla actions force Colombian food prices up.

text.p: Food prices have rocketed in Bogota since leftist guerrillas unleashed a massive offensive at the end of last month, according to a survey by Colombia's leading daily newspaper on Monday.

Since the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia and the National Liberation Army attempted to place a stranglehold on cities by blocking roads and burning trucks, the price of potatoes has risen by almost 40 percent and onions are double what they cost in late August.
The effect on other staples such as rice and eggs has been less dramatic, between four and six percent, but still well above the average monthly rate of inflation of about 1.5 percent.

The survey by El Tiempo calculated the cost of the basic food basket had risen more than 10 percent in the past month. It said port towns on the Caribbean coast and northeastern provinces had also been hard hit by the rebel blockade.

A spokesman for the Colombian truckers federation, Colfecar, said: "Undoubtedly guerrilla actions have been one factor in the price rises of the last month. As they destroy our cargoes we have to pass the costs on. But the problem also stems from well before because the rise in common crime has gone unchecked."

The nationwide rebel offensive, described by the authorities as one of the bloodiest in recent memory, began on Aug. 30 when guerrillas overran a military base in southern Putumayo province. More than 150 members of the security forces and civilians have died since then.
In the last few days, the military and police have begun to escort trucks along the country's most perilous highways in an effort to defend them from attack.
